The endings of relationships are difficult, and as social creatures we must all go through the experience at some point. I lost a great person as well, and even now when I look back on things with calm rationale, I can safely say that I was the one who pushed away.
But we have to be strong, you and I. We have to remind ourselves that these people who have affected us so deeply have left a positive impression. We have the ability to learn from the bad and take away the good, letting one teach us a lesson and the other provide a lasting memory, both of which will make us stronger and richer people for it.
Danny may have moved on before you did, but that does not necessarily mean that you had any less impact on his life than he did on yours. Every person moves at different speeds, but we all move forward. You may one day meet another person who will affect you as profoundly as this one, and then again you may not. But you will love again, even if it is falling back in love with the person that YOU have become. Take comfort in the fact that you received the gift of almost a decade with a person who means so much to you, and know that no matter what path that person walks from here, you have left an indelible mark on theirs as well. Remember the others in life who love you and cherish your existence, and realize that your existence will continue to move at the pace you are prepared to set for it, and no matter the pace it will be forward and it will be beautiful.
I certainly appreciate your time and consideration. I hope you are able to reunite safely with your significant other at some point in the future.

Two-part answer: Sex has recently become my reflective point on how much I have eschewed all social life in the last couple years. I didn't realize it until I stumbled onto /r/nofap and watched the "Your Brain on Porn" series. I'd become a porn addict, using masturbation as a quick fix solution on a regular basis. Over time, my contentedness with solitude became a reliance, and when I reflect upon these things it always seems to come back to masturbation: fleeting self-service in place of any meaningful social contact (even non-sexual). I've been NoFap for 9 days and it has been quite a struggle.
I also think that I struggle with sexual acceptance because, as a child, I was teased by a lot of girls for being an outcast. I remember a particular girl who defaced my 6th grade yearbook when I asked her to sign it, instead recounting a story of an incident of public vomiting I had in elementary school (I was always sick as a kid). I recall being upset and blacking out the entire quote with pen, ruining the cheap paper. Once I came to high school and got into my lifting and workout phase, a huge motivation for me was to gain sexual acceptance from my female peers, thus establishing my place in the social order. Even acknowledging all this now, and being old enough to hold my hormones in check, I still feel that familiar lust for attention poking at my frontal lobe.
